samples.reason: Authentic two-speaker point-at-issue anchor — Laird/Kim disagreement, credited answer is a proposition both speakers take a position on.

question.difficultyReason: Two speakers, both making nuanced multi-part claims. Trap (E) is a common 'point of agreement misread as disagreement' lure.
question.stimulus: Laird: Pure research provides us with new technologies that contribute to saving lives. Even more worthwhile than this, however, is its role in expanding our knowledge and providing new, unexplored ideas. Kim: Your priorities are mistaken. Saving lives is what counts most of all. Without pure research, medicine would not be as advanced as it is.
question.questionStem: Laird and Kim disagree on whether pure research

choices.label: A
choices.text: derives its significance in part from its providing new technologies

choices.label: B
choices.text: expands the boundaries of our knowledge of medicine

choices.label: C
choices.text: should have the saving of human lives as an important goal

choices.label: D
choices.text: has its most valuable achievements in medical applications

choices.label: E
choices.text: has any value apart from its role in providing new technologies to save lives

explanations.correct: Laird ranks expanding knowledge above saving lives; Kim says saving lives is what counts most. That is exactly a disagreement about whether the most valuable achievements of pure research are medical/life-saving applications.
explanations.A: Both agree pure research provides life-saving technology — no disagreement here.
explanations.C: Both could accept that saving lives is an important goal; they disagree about relative priority, not whether it is a goal at all.
explanations.E: Laird explicitly affirms pure research has value apart from life-saving; Kim does not clearly deny it. The trap is assuming Kim's 'what counts most' rules out other value.

source.notes: Stimulus, stem, and all five answer choices are verbatim from LSAC's public LR sample page. Correct answer D confirmed by LSAC's own rationale.
